citation: US 7,842,696 B2. Acetylation of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride and pyridine in dichloromethane. Reaction mined into the Open Reaction Database as ord-554541e1f28f476d9ed9cf5c41144fe2 (dataset DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.5104873.v1).
procedure: Written out at the scale the patent ran. Charge salicylic acid (0.72 mmol) and dichloromethane (10 mL) and cool the flask in an ice bath. Add pyridine (0.80 mmol, 1.1 equiv) to the cooled mixture. After 5 minutes add acetic anhydride (1.09 mmol, 1.5 equiv). Remove the ice bath and stir at room temperature for 4 hours. The product was extracted with dichloromethane and water, and the organic layer was washed with brine, dried over sodium sulfate and concentrated under reduced pressure to afford 2-acetoxybenzoic acid. On the printed amounts: the patent prints 10 mg beside 0.72 mmol for the salicylic acid and 10 microlitres beside 1.09 mmol for the acetic anhydride. 10 mg of salicylic acid is 0.072 mmol and 10 microlitres of acetic anhydride is 0.106 mmol, so both printed figures sit a factor of ten below the moles written next to them, while the pyridine agrees exactly (64 microlitres is 0.80 mmol). The mole figures are the self-consistent ones and are the basis used here; they put the run at about 99 mg of salicylic acid in 10 mL of dichloromethane. Nothing in this entry is estimated - every quantity is the patent's own mole figure, or that figure multiplied by a molar mass.
